Based on the provided context, here is a Semgrep rule that matches the vulnerable code structure:

```yaml
rules:
- id: "vuln-knowage-server-f7d0362f"
  pattern: $CLASS.checkJNDIName($IDataSource)
  pattern-not: $CLASS.checkJNDIName(sanitized_dataSource)
  pattern-inside: |
    class $CLASS {
      ...
      private void checkJNDIName(IDataSource dataSource) {
        ...
      }
    }
  languages: ["java"]
  message: |
    Potential JNDI injection vulnerability. 
    The `checkJNDIName` method is used to validate the JNDI name of a data source. 
    If the JNDI name does not start with "java:comp/env/jdbc/", an exception is thrown. 
    This could potentially lead to unauthorized access to sensitive data. 
    To fix this, sanitize the JNDI name to ensure it starts with "java:comp/env/jdbc/".
  severity: ERROR
  metadata:
    source-url: github.com/KnowageLabs/Knowage-Server/commit/f7d0362f737e1b0db1cc9cc95b1236d62d83dd0c
    category: security
    cwe: [CWE-915]
    owasp: [OWASP A3:2017-Injection]
    references: [https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Injection/]
    technology: [java]
```

This rule will match any occurrence of `checkJNDIName` method call with an argument that is not a sanitized version. The `pattern-inside` field is used to limit the match to specific code blocks. The `pattern-not` field is used to exclude the fixed version of the pattern. The `metadata` field contains additional context like the source URL, category, CWE number, OWASP category, references, and technology.

Please note that the CWE number and OWASP category are based on general knowledge and might not be accurate for this specific vulnerability. You should update them based on the actual vulnerability.
